I will not start from zero. I have farmed here many years, so I will do close to what worked for me last year and what I see around me in Quzhou. Cotton is still my backbone crop, so I will keep the biggest area there because it is steadier than chili. Chili can make money, but it eats fertilizer, water, and spraying money, so I will not spread it too wide with only myself at home. Mungbean costs less and is easier to manage, so I will keep a smaller piece for cash flow and to lighten the fertilizer bill. With well irrigation, I do not need to fear drought too much, so I will feed chili and cotton a bit heavier rather than risk weak growth. On 10.1 mu, every bag of fertilizer and every spray round matters, so I will hold mungbean low-input, keep cotton in the middle, and put the better seed and more water into chili where the return is usually higher if the stand is good.
